# S51 — Make auto-backup exclusion explicit

**Findings:** res/xml/backup_rules.xml and res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml (template files with TODOs); AndroidManifest.xml (allowBackup=false) · **Size:** S · **Tree:** release

**Not in this slice:** enabling any form of Android backup or device transfer. The owner decided it stays disabled.

## Why

The manifest sets `allowBackup="false"` but still points at the Android Studio template rule files, which are comments and a TODO. The behaviour is correct, but it relies on a single flag and the files look unfinished. Explicit rules make the intent deterministic and lint-clean.

## Files

- `app/src/main/res/xml/backup_rules.xml`
- `app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml`
- `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (read only: keep `allowBackup="false"`)

## Failing tests

- None. Lint is the check.

## Implement

1. `backup_rules.xml`:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
   <full-backup-content>
       <exclude domain="root" path="." />
       <exclude domain="file" path="." />
       <exclude domain="database" path="." />
       <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." />
       <exclude domain="external" path="." />
   </full-backup-content>
   ```
2. `data_extraction_rules.xml`: put the same five `<exclude>` lines inside both `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>`.
3. Keep `allowBackup="false"` and both attributes in the manifest.
4. `PRIVACY.md` already says automatic Android backup is disabled, so it needs no change.

## Check

- `./gradlew lintDebug` reports no new warnings, and none about backup or data extraction rules.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` passes and the app launches.
